clue.text: A leather bit one put in order again

definitions.text: A leather bit one put in order again

indicators.note: putting things in order means arranging them afresh, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone repairs a piece of harness by setting a strip of leather straight again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in order' rearranges A LEATHER BIT plus I (one); the whole clue also describes mending the harness, so it doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehabilitate is to restore something to good condition, putting it right once more.

clue.text: Ronald's a rising physician or poet

parts.note: Ron is short for Ronald, with the possessive s kept

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means the doctor's letters read upwards

parts.note: Dr is short for doctor

explanation.surface: A man named Ronald is a doctor climbing the ladder, or perhaps a versifier.
explanation.walkthrough: Pierre de Ronsard was a sixteenth-century French poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierre de Ronsard led the Pléiade group of French Renaissance poets.

clue.text: Jack the Bat holds it for Frodo & Co

indicators.note: the cricketer's name contains the other word

parts.note: Sir Jack Hobbs was a great English cricketer, a famous batsman

explanation.surface: A man called Jack the Bat keeps something for Frodo and his friends.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Hobbs was England's great opening batsman of the 1910s and 1920s; 'Bat' looks like an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Frodo and his companions are the small halfling folk of Tolkien's tales.

clue.text: Apollonian viewpoint

parts.note: the famous Vatican statue of Apollo is named after the lookout court where it stood

explanation.walkthrough: The Apollo Belvedere is a celebrated statue; a belvedere is also a raised turret or summerhouse with a view.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a structure built to command a fine view, and names a classical statue of Apollo.

clue.text: Tongue the Bard had little of, wrote Ben

definitions.text: Tongue the Bard had little of, wrote Ben

parts.words: Tongue the Bard had little of, wrote Ben
parts.note: Ben Jonson said Shakespeare had small knowledge of one classical language and less Greek

explanation.walkthrough: Ben Jonson's tribute says Shakespeare (the Bard) had 'small Latine and lesse Greeke'.
explanation.definitionFit: The language of ancient Rome is the one Jonson said Shakespeare knew only slightly.

clue.text: The careless gunman is so happy

definitions.text: The careless gunman is so happy

parts.words: The careless gunman is so happy
parts.note: a gunman too quick to shoot is described with a compound ending in happy

explanation.walkthrough: The compound 'trigger-happy' means quick to shoot; 'happy' looks like cheerfulness.
explanation.definitionFit: The firing lever of a gun gives its name to the word for someone rash with firearms.

clue.text: Winged sandals for the part of the immortal Ariadne

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Footwear with wings suits the role of the deathless Ariadne.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts in the last letters of 'immortal' and continues into 'Ariadne'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Hermes wears flying footwear called by this Latin name.

clue.text: Cassandra's Wild West reincarnation ?

parts.note: Cassandra prophesied disaster, and a frontierswoman of the Old West was nicknamed after disaster

explanation.walkthrough: Cassandra foretold doom at Troy; Martha Jane Canary, the frontier scout, was known by a nickname meaning a disaster-prone woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The frontierswoman's nickname links her to disaster, as Cassandra was linked to foretelling ruin.

clue.text: Miss Lee of poetic fame

parts.note: the title maiden of Edgar Allan Poe's last poem, whose surname is Lee

explanation.walkthrough: Edgar Allan Poe's poem about a lost love 'in a kingdom by the sea' is named for her.
explanation.definitionFit: The heroine of Poe's ballad is a young woman named in its title with the surname Lee.

clue.text: Vacancy notice is about right-one in eight lines

indicators.note: the notice goes round the other letters, so 'is about' puts them inside it

parts.note: TO LET is the sign on an empty property
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A landlord's sign is concerned with being correct, set in a short poem.
explanation.walkthrough: TO LET is the British notice on a house or room for rent; R and I sit inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A triolet is a verse form of eight lines with two rhymes and repeated refrains.

clue.text: Farson's sinner had a way with him

definitions.text: Farson's sinner had a way with him

parts.words: Farson's sinner had a way with him
parts.note: Negley Farson's memoir is called The Way of a ..., naming a wrongdoer

explanation.walkthrough: Negley Farson's 1935 autobiography is 'The Way of a Transgressor'; 'had a way with him' sounds like charm.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinner is one who breaks moral law, the figure in the title of Farson's memoir.

clue.text: A lady embracing Italian nudist

indicators.note: an embrace wraps around, so the lady's title holds the other letters

parts.note: a dame is a titled lady
It is short for Italian, as in gin and It (Italian vermouth)

explanation.surface: A woman hugs an Italian who goes about without clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: The Adamites were early Christian sects who went naked in imitation of Adam before the Fall.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the sect named after the first man worshipped unclothed, so the word came to mean a naturist.

clue.text: Yorkshire's river spirit found back in Africa

indicators.note: back means the pieces are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: the Aire is a river flowing through Leeds in Yorkshire
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: A Yorkshire river's ghost turns up again on another continent.
explanation.walkthrough: The Aire is a Yorkshire river; 'back' reverses both pieces together. 'spirit' looks supernatural but is the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The country is a West African state, so it is something found on that continent.

clue.text: It flows in many states

parts.note: a great river of South Asia running through several countries

explanation.walkthrough: The river rises in Tibet and runs through India and Pakistan; 'states' looks like American states but means nations.
explanation.definitionFit: The great river of Pakistan crosses several national territories on its way to the Arabian Sea.

clue.text: Bears arms in order to disconcert people

indicators.note: putting things in order rearranges them, so these letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Someone takes up weapons to unsettle the public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in order' rearranges BEARS ARMS; 'Bears arms' looks like a soldier's action.
explanation.definitionFit: To make others feel awkward or ashamed is to discomfit or unsettle them.

clue.text: Rests after exertion for those surviving

definitions.meaning: short pauses to recover one's wind
living people, who still draw air

explanation.definitionFit: Short pauses to catch one's wind, and people still alive and drawing air.

clue.text: When the outlook was dark very recently

definitions.text: When the outlook was dark very recently

parts.words: When the outlook was dark very recently
parts.note: the darkness is nightfall, and the recent time is the evening just past

explanation.walkthrough: The 'dark outlook' suggests gloom, but it is simply dusk falling the day before.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for the evening of the previous day, when it last grew dark.

clue.text: Decide to include a USA port

indicators.note: the word for decide takes the other letter inside it

parts.note: to settle a matter is to decide it

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to add an American harbour to the itinerary.
explanation.definitionFit: Seattle is a major harbour city in Washington State on Puget Sound.

clue.text: I have to save up first — such is my excuse

indicators.note: first says this piece comes before the other
in a down entry up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: Someone explains they must put money by first, a shifty excuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the saving word and 'first' puts it ahead; the definition describes an excuse that dodges, read as the speaker's own admission.
explanation.definitionFit: An excuse that dodges the real question is shifty and slippery.

clue.text: Peter the alliterative musician

definitions.meaning: the tongue-twister hero who picked a peck of pickled peppers
a player of pipes or bagpipes

explanation.definitionFit: Peter of the nursery tongue-twister shares a surname with someone who plays the pipes.

clue.text: Soft like land for the sower and the seed for example

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical abbreviation for soft
land fit for ploughing and sowing is described as arable

explanation.surface: Gentle, like ground ready for the farmer and his seed.
explanation.walkthrough: The Parable of the Sower in the Gospels tells of seed falling on different ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A Gospel story such as the one about scattered seed is a moral tale told by Jesus.

clue.text: Submarine star

definitions.meaning: a class of nuclear missile boat named after its missile

explanation.definitionFit: The North Star gave its name to a ballistic missile and the submarines carrying it.

clue.text: Language of Hindu hero, one in a hundred

indicators.note: in says the hero and the one go inside the other pair of letters

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
Rama is the hero of the Hindu epic the Ramayana
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: The tongue of an Indian epic hero is a rare thing, one in a hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one in a hundred' reads as a phrase for rarity, but A and C enclose RAMA and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Aramaic is the ancient Semitic tongue of the Near East, spoken by Jesus.

clue.text: It's green and tasty with mustard

definitions.text: It's green and tasty with mustard

parts.words: It's green and tasty with mustard
parts.note: a salad plant traditionally paired with mustard sprouts in British sandwiches

explanation.walkthrough: 'Mustard and cress' is a British salad of seedlings grown together; the mustard is the plant, not the condiment.
explanation.definitionFit: A peppery salad seedling eaten in sandwiches alongside sprouted mustard.

clue.text: What a switchback gives us -shirt ruined, about two pounds

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the other piece
a ruined garment is wrecked, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound, so two make LL

explanation.surface: A fairground ride leaves a shirt torn, costing a couple of quid.
explanation.walkthrough: A switchback is a British name for a roller coaster. 'ruined' rearranges the shirt's letters and 'about' wraps them round the two pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A roller coaster provides excitement and sudden rushes of fear and delight.

clue.text: Tolkien's tree-man taking drink seems to weave in and out

parts.note: the Ents are the tree-giants of The Lord of the Rings
wine is a drink

explanation.surface: A Tolkien tree-giant who has had a drink appears to stagger about.
explanation.walkthrough: The tree-man's apparent weaving is drunken staggering, but the definition is interlacing threads.
explanation.definitionFit: To intertwine is to twist strands round one another, passing in and out.

clue.text: "O hold me tight! " turns into a "Stop "order

indicators.note: turns says the whole phrase is read backwards to make the answer

parts.note: to grab is to seize and hold

explanation.surface: A lover's cry for an embrace becomes a command to halt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns into' reverses O + GRAB + ME as one run; 'tight' just completes the lover's plea.
explanation.definitionFit: An official ban halting trade with a country is an order to cease.

clue.text: London's road stars

explanation.definitionFit: A north London road and the Pleiades cluster share the same name.
